# ForgeDNA — llms.txt
# AI Agent & LLM Integration Reference
# Last updated: 2025
# Homepage: https://forgedna.replit.app

## PLATFORM OVERVIEW

ForgeDNA is a text-first VR game design platform. Creators design, remix, share,
and manage VR game blueprints as structured JSON documents called "GameDNA."
The platform serves as a community hub and schema workbench — actual game
compilation and generation happens on external infrastructure using AI agents
and game engines like Godot.

GameDNA schemas are engine-agnostic, human-readable, and AI-friendly. They
describe everything about a VR game: environment physics, player rig, entities,
game logic, levels, and audio.

## HOW TO USE THE PLATFORM

### Web Interface
- Homepage: / — Platform overview, featured schemas, quick-start
- Databanks (Gallery): /schemas — Browse, search, filter, star, and fork public schemas
- Schema Editor: /schemas/:id/edit — 8-tab visual editor for GameDNA schemas
- Schema Detail: /schemas/:id — View schema details, extract JSON, fork
- Build Guide: /guide — Comprehensive implementation guide for AI agents and Godot
- WebXR Play: /play/:slug — Play a schema in WebXR directly in browser

### Core Workflows
1. CREATE a new schema from scratch or from a genre template
2. EDIT using the 8-tab editor (Meta, Environment, Player Rig, Entities, Logic, Levels, Audio, JSON)
3. GENERATE a Godot 4.x project using the built-in deterministic generator or AI agent swarm
4. EXPORT the GameDNA JSON to feed into your own AI agent pipeline
5. SHARE by making schemas public, allowing others to fork and remix
6. PLAY via WebXR preview or export to VR headsets

### Genre Templates
Pre-built starting points available when creating new schemas:
- Survival Sandbox
- Puzzle Platformer
- Horror Escape Room
- Space Exploration
- Combat Arena
- Social Hub

## GAMEDNA SCHEMA STRUCTURE

Every GameDNA schema is organized into 7 top-level sections ("pillars"):

### 1. meta
Game metadata: title, description, slug, genre, target platforms, version.

### 2. environment_config
World settings: physics (gravity vector, drag), lighting (type, color, intensity,
shadows), skybox, fog, post-processing effects, world boundaries.

### 3. player_rig
VR player configuration: height, movement (locomotion type, speed, jump, snap-turn),
hand interaction (grab distance, haptic feedback), comfort settings (vignette,
teleport), collision shape.

### 4. entity_registry
Array of game entities. Each entity has:
- id: Unique string identifier
- label: Display name
- mesh: 3D model reference (primitive or path)
- transform: Position, rotation, scale
- physics: Body type, mass, collision shape
- tags: Categorization array
- scripts: Attached behavior scripts
- components: Additional data components

### 5. logic_recipes
Game logic definitions as event-driven recipes:
- id: Recipe identifier
- label: Human-readable name
- trigger: Event that activates the recipe (collision, timer, input, proximity)
- conditions: Array of conditions that must be true
- actions: Array of actions to execute (spawn, destroy, modify, teleport, play_sound)
- target_entity_id: Which entity this recipe applies to

### 6. levels
Level/scene definitions:
- id: Level identifier
- label: Display name
- spawn_point: Player spawn position and rotation
- entity_ids: Array of entity IDs placed in this level
- environment_overrides: Per-level environment setting overrides

### 7. audio
Audio configuration:
- music_tracks: Background music definitions
- sfx_library: Sound effect definitions with trigger mappings
- spatial_audio: 3D audio settings
- ambient: Ambient sound layers

## API REFERENCE

Base URL: /api

### Health
GET /api/healthz — Health check, returns server status

### Authentication
GET /api/auth/user — Get the currently authenticated user
GET /api/login — Start browser OIDC login flow (redirects)
GET /api/callback — OIDC callback handler
GET /api/logout — Clear session and logout
POST /api/mobile-auth/token-exchange — Exchange mobile OIDC code for session
POST /api/mobile-auth/logout — Delete mobile session token

### GameDNA Schemas
GET /api/schemas — List public schemas (supports query params: search, genre, sort, limit, offset)
POST /api/schemas — Create a new schema (auth required, body: title, description, schema JSON)
GET /api/schemas/game-dna — Get the canonical GameDNA JSON Schema contract
GET /api/schemas/mine — List current user's schemas (auth required)
GET /api/schemas/:id — Get a single schema by ID
PUT /api/schemas/:id — Update a schema (auth required, owner only)
DELETE /api/schemas/:id — Delete a schema (auth required, owner only)

### Schema Social Features
POST /api/schemas/:id/fork — Fork a public schema (auth required)
POST /api/schemas/:id/star — Star/bookmark a schema (auth required)
DELETE /api/schemas/:id/star — Remove star from a schema (auth required)

### Schema Versioning
GET /api/schemas/:id/versions — List version history for a schema
POST /api/schemas/:id/versions/restore — Restore to a previous version (auth required, body: versionId)

### Godot Project Generation (Deterministic)
POST /api/parse — Generate a Godot 4.x project ZIP from GameDNA JSON (body: schema JSON)
GET /api/parse/status/:jobId — Poll generation job status
GET /api/parse/download/:jobId — Download generated Godot project ZIP

### AI Agent Build (AI-Powered Generation)
POST /api/ai-build — Start AI-powered Godot build using agent swarm (auth required, body: schemaId)
GET /api/ai-build/stream/:jobId — Stream agent build logs via Server-Sent Events (SSE)
GET /api/ai-build/status/:jobId — Poll AI build job status
GET /api/ai-build/download/:jobId — Download AI-generated Godot project ZIP

### Cloud Build (Simulated)
POST /api/cloud-build — Queue a cloud Godot export build (auth required)
GET /api/cloud-build/:buildId — Get cloud build status

### WebXR Play
GET /api/play/:slug — Get play/WebXR data for a schema by its slug

## MCP (MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL) TOOLS

ForgeDNA's AI agent pipeline uses three MCP tools for iterative game generation:

### Tool: read_game_dna
Read a specific section of the GameDNA schema JSON.
Parameters:
  - section (string, required): One of "meta", "environment_config", "player_rig",
    "entity_registry", "logic_recipes", "levels", "audio", "full"
Returns: The requested section of the schema as JSON.

### Tool: write_gdscript
Write a GDScript (.gd) file to the Godot project.
Parameters:
  - file_path (string, required): Relative path, e.g. "scripts/player_locomotion.gd"
  - content (string, required): Full GDScript source code
  - description (string, required): Brief description of what this script does
  - target_entity_id (string, required): Entity ID from entity_registry to attach to
  - node_type (string, optional): Godot node type — one of "Node", "Node3D", "Area3D",
    "CharacterBody3D", "RigidBody3D", "StaticBody3D". Defaults to "Node".
  - attach_mode (string, optional): "root" (attach to entity root node) or "child"
    (create new child node). Defaults to "child".

### Tool: write_tscn
Write a Godot scene (.tscn) file to the project.
Parameters:
  - file_path (string, required): Relative path, e.g. "scenes/craft_station.tscn"
  - content (string, required): Full Godot text scene file content
  - description (string, required): Brief description of what this scene contains

### Agent Loop Pattern
1. Read the "meta" section to understand the game concept
2. Read "environment_config" to set up the world
3. Read "player_rig" to configure VR player
4. Read "entity_registry" to enumerate all game entities
5. For each entity, write_tscn to create its scene file
6. Read "logic_recipes" and write_gdscript for each recipe's behavior
7. Read "levels" to set up level scenes
8. Read "audio" to configure sound
9. Self-validate by re-reading schema and comparing against generated files
